headline: Southbury inspection steps.
subhead: A four-step checklist for buying a home with private systems in Southbury. Swipe.

slides.title: Book standard mechanicals first.
slides.text: Have a licensed inspector check the roof, foundation, heating system, electrical panel, and plumbing fixtures for age and wear.

slides.title: Test the private well.
slides.text: Many Southbury homes use private wells. Run a potability water test in a lab and verify the pump flow rate.

slides.title: Open and pump septic.
slides.text: Hire a dedicated septic technician to locate the tank, inspect baffles, check leach fields, and pump the system completely.

slides.title: Run radon air tests.
slides.text: Place continuous monitors in the lowest finished space for forty-eight hours to measure baseline radon gas levels accurately.

slides.title: Negotiate repairs or credits.
slides.text: Use the written inspection reports before your contract deadline to ask the seller for direct credits or necessary fixes.

recap: Lab water test and well flow
Full septic tank and leach field

caption:
Inspecting a house in Southbury CT is different than checking out a condo downtown.

Most properties here have private wells and on-site septic tanks. That means your standard home inspection is only step one. You need a dedicated septic tech to pull the tank lid, inspect the baffles, and evaluate the absorption field. You also want a certified lab test for your drinking water flow and quality.

Don't skip the continuous radon monitor in the basement either. Getting these reports in hand before your contingency deadline gives you clean leverage to request seller credits.

If you're planning a purchase, comment BUY and I'll send you homes for sale right now in Southbury.
